title: fix(plugin-auth)!: admin create-user refuses a password outside the deployment's length range
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-elon-musk"} -->
_Requested by **Elon** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9D?thread=cmsg_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9D35eCXEFgjdFBa5wrMSFZSx)_
Fixes #25824

Clause-②: no (narrowing) — admin create-user refuses one request shape it used to run: an explicit `password` shorter than the deployment's `minPasswordLength` (one longer than `maxPasswordLength` was already refused by better-auth, now with set-user-password's code). Nothing is widened.
Metadata-protocol: none

## Why

`POST /api/v1/auth/admin/create-user` saved a 1-character password, and the user then signed in with it (the card's repro, measured on a stock showcase boot). `set-user-password` refuses the same value with `400 INVALID_REQUEST` "Password must be at least 8 characters", and the user's own change-password refuses it with `400 PASSWORD_TOO_SHORT`. The cause is in better-auth 1.7.12 itself: `admin/create-user` runs `assertPasswordNotTooLong` only, while `admin/set-user-password` runs both `assertPasswordNotTooShort` and `assertPasswordNotTooLong` (`better-auth/dist/plugins/admin/routes.mjs`, read in this worktree's install). Our `runAdminCreateUser` passed the password straight to that `createUser`. Our `resolvePassword` ran only the complexity check, and the length check lived only in the set-user-password runner. ADR-0069 records `password_min_length` / `password_max_length` → `emailAndPassword.minPasswordLength` / `maxPasswordLength` as enforced, and on this door it was not.

## What changed (`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/admin-user-endpoints.ts`)

- **One length check, in the one place both admin doors resolve a credential.** `resolvePassword` now takes the deployment's range (`AuthContextLike['password']['config']`, better-auth's resolved `minPasswordLength` / `maxPasswordLength`). It refuses a password outside that range with set-user-password's existing refusal: `400 INVALID_REQUEST`, "Password must be at least N characters" / "Password must be at most N characters". There is no new error code. set-user-password's own copy of the check is deleted, so the two doors cannot drift apart again.
- **create-user reads the range before anything is written.** It reads `getAuthContext()` before `resolvePassword`, so a refusal comes before the multi-org join check, the permission-set grant, `createUser`, the must-change stamp and the audit row. If the context cannot be read, the request is refused through `mapAuthApiError` (`create-user failed`) and no account is created. That is the same mapping set-user-password already used for the same read.
- **A generated password is sized to the range.** It is `min(max(16, minPasswordLength), maxPasswordLength)` long, and `generateTemporaryPassword` still never goes below 12. Before, it was always 16. So with a minimum above 16, set-user-password refused the password it had just generated, and create-user saved it below the minimum. The range check runs on generated passwords too, so one that still cannot fit (a maximum below 12) is refused, never saved.
- Check order on set-user-password is unchanged: `userId`, then complexity, then length. The one difference is that the context read moved ahead of password resolution, which is observable only when that read throws.

Changeset: `.changeset/25824-admin-create-user-password-length.md` (`@objectstack/plugin-auth` patch, BREAKING banner, ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, before / now / fix).

## Verification

- **New pins** (`admin-user-endpoints.test.ts`, describe "admin doors: one password length range"), run across both doors from one table:
  - Refusal pins: `'a'` (the repro), one short of the minimum, one past the maximum. Each answers `400`, `INVALID_REQUEST` and the exact message, and writes nothing (no `createUser`, no hash, no account write, no engine update, no audit insert).
  - Boundary pins: exactly the minimum and exactly the maximum are applied.
  - Configured-range pin: a configured `minPasswordLength: 12` refuses a 10-character password.
  - Generated-password pins: a minimum of 24 gives a 24-character password, and a maximum of 14 gives a 14-character one.
  - create-user only: an unreadable auth context refuses with no account.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/admin-user-endpoints.test.ts src/durability-swallow-repair.test.ts`: VERDICT command-exit 0, 2 files, 115/115.

  - **A** (the range check deleted from `resolvePassword`): 9 failed / 84 passed. All six refusal pins (both doors), both configured-range pins, and the pre-existing "enforces better-auth min password length" went red.

## Claim race on the card

Two `Claim:` comments landed 88 s apart: this seat's 6407745341 (03:45:06Z) and `domain:server` seat 1's 6407761859 (03:46:34Z, read against a stale "unassigned" card). Seat 1 withdrew in 6407776655, and the seat's arbitration is 6407784753. This PR is the 6407745341 claim's. Seat 1's thread made no edit and opens no PR.

## Acceptance notes

- **Admin import-users is not sized to the range** (noted, not filed: reach not measured live). With `passwordPolicy: 'temporary'`, `admin-import-users.ts` calls `generateTemporaryPassword()` with no length, and its deps carry no auth context. On a deployment whose `minPasswordLength` is above 16, a temporary-password import would save 16-character credentials below the minimum, the same way create-user did, because better-auth's `createUser` checks only the maximum. This is the same defect class, but it is in another file outside this claim's surface. Dedupe words: import-users temporary password minPasswordLength, generateTemporaryPassword length import.
- **Two codes for one policy.** The admin doors answer `INVALID_REQUEST` (set-user-password's existing code, kept per the triage route "with the same code"), while better-auth's sign-up and change-password answer `PASSWORD_TOO_SHORT` / `PASSWORD_TOO_LONG`. Aligning them would change a wire answer, so it is out of scope here.
- On both admin doors the complexity check still runs before the length check, as on set-user-password before. A short password that also fails complexity gets the complexity refusal.
